new_clusters.summary: The rating field's .nullable()...optional() split replaces the previous .nullish() purely because .refine() had to be inserted between the modifiers, leaving the declaration stylistically out of step with the sibling rating fields in search.dto.ts and exif.dto.ts.

Re-adopting -1 as an out-of-band 'rejected' sentinel inside a 1-5 ordinal happens at the one moment retiring it was cheapest (an unreleased major with the breaking change and backfill already written), forcing every consumer to special-case it and pushing removal to a second major bump.

The rating field on UpdateAssetBaseSchema backs AssetBulkUpdateDto as well, but the bulk-update spec block never sends a rating at all, so that DTO's rating validation has no test coverage of any value (pre-existing).

Placing .describe() and .meta() after the new .refine() was checked for attaching to the wrong schema node; both attach correctly and the description plus x-immich-history extension appear as expected in the generated spec.
The refine predicate's accepted value set was enumerated against the stated intent: null, -1 and 1..5 accept while 0, -2, 6 and 3.5 reject, matching exactly.
The unchanged x-immich-state 'Stable' marker was checked against the edited history chain and remains correct, because the extension is derived from the last non-Added/Updated entry.
SyncAssetExifV1.rating is declared z.int().nullable() with no bounds, so the delta-sync surface already tolerates -1 and mirrors the DB column deliberately — no drift is introduced.

The client-side half of the original restriction is not reverted: the Dart widgets, action/search models and web StarRating.svelte that were changed to stop sending -1 remain as-is, so first-party clients still cannot set a rejection even though the API now accepts it.

The rating validity rule is written inline at four sites with now-divergent rulesets (asset.dto.ts, exif.dto.ts, search.dto.ts, sync.dto.ts) instead of a shared schema constant like the file's own latitudeSchema/longitudeSchema, which is what let the definitions drift apart.
The sidecar write path maps rating ?? 0 when emitting XMP, which is pre-existing and coherent with the extraction side's 0 -> null mapping.

The extraction that nulls the rating was checked for re-queuing another sidecar write and thus a self-amplifying job loop; no AssetExtractMetadata -> SidecarWrite edge exists, so the chain terminates after one round trip.
The asset_exif.rating column carries no CHECK constraint or non-null bound, so the range restriction was always application-level and re-permitting -1 implies no database schema work.
The deleted migration performed a data UPDATE with no DDL, so removing it introduces no code-first schema or snapshot drift.
The new field-level refine passes its message via `error:` while the untouched object-level lat/long refine uses `message:`; both are supported and the mixed usage predates the diff.

The tree was swept for dangling references to the deleted migration — no manifest, index, seed or doc names it — confirming the breakage lives in the recorded database row rather than in the repository.
